rules_text:
Rules summary It's a game. There are boxes. You need luck. And it's Super Mega. Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 3 Scoring 4 Solo Rules Overview The objective of the game is to cross off all the numbers on your lucky box cards. Complete rows and columns to earn points and bonus actions. Each round, nine number cards will be drawn from an 18-card deck. Each card is numbered 1 through 9 twice. For each card drawn, cross off a matching number on one of your lucky box cards. After 4 rounds, see who was luckiest! Gameplay At the beginning of the game, choose 3 of the 5 lucky box cards available. Then the top card of the deck is revealed. Click that number on any of your Lucky Box cards to cross it off. When you cross off all three numbers on a row or column, gain the bonus action shown in the box at the end. Bonuses are: Number : You may cross that number off in another box. Question mark : You may cross off any number in another box. Lightning bolt(s) : Take one or two Lightning tokens from the supply. Star : Used in scoring for the round. Moon : Used in scoring the end of the game. Lightning tokens can be used to increase or decrease the number on the card being played by 1 for each lightning token used. For example, if a 4 is drawn, you can spend one lightning token to cross off a 5 or a 3, or spend two lightning tokens to score 6 or 2. The number 9 can wrap around to 1 and vice versa. You cannot use lighting tokens to adjust a number given through a bonus action. Scoring Each completed Lucky Box card scores points based on the round it was completed: Round 1 = 15 points for each card Round 2 = 12 points for each card Round 3 = 10 points for each card Round 4 = 8 points for each card Stars earn points based on how many you gain in a round. 1 star = 1 point 2 stars = 4 points 3 or more stars = 9 points At the end of the game, the player with the MOST moons earns 6 points. The player with the FEWEST moons loses 6 points (except in a two-player game). In case of a tie for moons, all tied players gain or lose the full 6 points. Finally, gain 1 point for every 2 crossed-out boxes on incomplete Lucky Box cards. The player with the most points wins the game! In case of a tie, the player with the most moons wins. Solo Rules You can have a party all by yourself! Rules are the same except for the moon scoring at the end: 0 moons = -6 points 1 moon = -2 points 2 moons = 0 points 3 moons = 1 point 4 moons = 3 points 5 moons = 6 points 6+ moons = 10 points Scoring Score Rating Under 44 Super Mega UN-lucky 45-59 OK, you got lucky, but not very 60-64 You got the hang of it now! 65-69 Super mega bragging rights! 70+ Super Mega Lucky Legend!

---

Your goal in Super Mega Lucky Box is to score as many points as possible, and you'll do that mostly by crossing off the nine numbers printed in a 3x3 grid on the cards in front of you.

During each of the four rounds, you shuffle 18 cards (numbered 1-9 twice), then reveal nine of those cards one by one. For each number revealed, you cross off a matching number on one of your cards, with you starting the game by choosing three out of five cards. Each time you complete a row or column, you receive the printed bonus next to it:


     A lightning bolt, which you can spend to raise or lower the number that you're crossing off on a turn; spend three lightning bolts, for example, and you can change a 7 into either a 4 or a 1 (because the numbers "wrap")
     A moon, with the player who has the most moons scoring 6 points at game's end, while the player with the fewest loses 6 points (except in a two-player game)
     A star, with you scoring 1, 4, or 9 points for collecting 1, 2, or 3 stars in a single round
     A number, which you immediately cross off on one of your cards; if doing so completes another row or column, you score that bonus, too!
     A question mark, which allows you to cross off any number.


At the end of a round, you score points for each card that you've completely marked off, with the points diminishing each round from 15 in round one to 8 in round four. Each player then draws three new cards and keeps one of them.

After four rounds, you score 1 point for each two spaces Xed on unfinished cards, then tally your points from completed cards, stars, and moons to see who has the highest score and wins.

[Rating: 2/10] The bingo boards are much smaller than I expected.   The game feels extremely luck-based, in particular which boards you can select from.  Some boards feel clearly better than others.   The game loop is boring and unengaging.  Players get nothing when a number is called and they can't play it anywhere. This is very punishing.  The game does not feel great at 2P as the moon moon bonus feels very beneficial.  Overall, I feel the winner of games is usually determined by who gets the best player boards to select from. This makes the game feel very bleh, and super luck based and not worth returning

[Rating: 2/10] Silly. Like, remarkably silly. Reminds me of those lottery scratch-off games. But also: Modestly amusing and…oddly addicting? (Just like those lottery scratch-off games…) And it’s snappy enough to subsist on nothing other than "amusing" and "addicting", so there’s that.

[Rating: 2/10] I kept coming back to it and I'm really not sure why. I really like Phil Walker-Harding's games--Sushi Go is among my favorites of all time--but this is by far the most asinine garbage I have ever played. To even dare to call it a game is pretentious. I did eventually score 74. There may be a small amount of skill, but I'm doubtful.

[Rating: 2/10] After one play on BGA: Bingo, advanced version. I guess it’s a matter of personal taste, but I really don’t like being so completely at the mercy of luck. This kind of external control triggers a deep aversion in me, even if it’s just a game. While the game does offer some room for decisions, I find it too limited. I get the uncomfortable feeling that the game is playing me, not the other way around.

[Rating: 3/10] Silver and Gold: now with 100% fewer polyominos and 100% more numbers. Scoring is the same, by which I mean it's artificially close and barely matters what you do, all your scores will converge by the end and a bonus or two will decide the winner.

[Rating: 3/10] This was a flip and write that I found quite boring and uninteresting.  Couple of different ways to score and you could collect more lightning chips to modify values a bit but it doesn't do anything fun.
